subject.title: fix(compaction): prevent repeated restarts after safety timeouts

question: Should embedded compaction be allowed to commit one typed partial summary after its safety timeout fires, provided the result arrives within the reason-owned settlement window and advances only across proven summarized entries?
rationale: Tests and runtime proof support the implementation, but accepting persisted session-state mutation after the caller has observed a timeout is an intentional product and ownership-policy choice that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve bounded partial commits
options.body: Accept the reason-owned settlement policy, rebase the branch, and require the focused session-state and lifecycle suites to pass on the final head.

options.title: Require pre-timeout commits only
options.body: Reject all results after timeout and redesign compaction around durable checkpoints committed before the wrapper reports failure.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Keep strict terminal timeout behavior and rely on larger configured budgets or a narrower future checkpoint design instead of post-timeout persistence.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded partial commits
recommendation.body: Accept the reason-owned settlement policy, rebase the branch, and require the focused session-state and lifecycle suites to pass on the final head.
